title: Kernel suggester via cost-gradient probing for arch+seqlen profiles
creator: Daniel Cho
description: Implement an online 'kernel suggester' that uses short cost-gradient probing to recommend the best kernel implementation for a given combination of model architecture, GPU family, and sequence-length bucket. The suggester will run low-cost microprobes and synthesize a local cost-gradient (delta latency / delta token-cost) for candidate kernels, producing a ranked suggestion plus confidence score. The goal is to reduce tail latency and per-token cost across mixed workloads while preserving safety (no regressions > SLO thresholds).
acceptance_criteria: Microprobe runner executes safely on-host with <0.5% additional request latency overhead during probing windows
Suggester outputs per-(model,arch,seqlen-bucket) recommendations + confidence stored in runtime catalog
Canary rollout shows >=3% median token-cost reduction or >=5% tail latency improvement for targeted workloads without SLO regressions
Automatic fallback to default kernel when confidence < threshold or when regression detected
Dashboard panels (prefill/decode split) show pick distribution, probe frequency, and regressions
implementation_notes: Probe design: run capped micro-batches (2-8 requests) across candidate kernels using shadow probes or low-priority lanes
Metric synthesis: compute cost-gradient as (latency + alpha*token-cost) differences; alpha tunable per-customer tier
Exploration policy: epsilon-greedy with decaying epsilon and safety guardrails using rolling regression detectors
Storage: write suggestions to a small in-memory catalog with TTL and versioning; persist occasional snapshots to S3 for analysis
Integration: expose suggestion API for serving runtime to consult before schedule decision; add signal for 'forced fallback' in emergency mode
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + simulator using production trace replay (local)
Phase 1 (internal): enable for internal traffic only, low probe rate (0.1% requests), collect telemetry
Phase 2 (canary): 5% customer traffic with strict rollback hooks if regressions detected
Phase 3 (ramp): increase to 25% then 100% with monitoring and gradual decay of exploration
telemetry_and_metrics: regression detectors: rolling z-score and p95 delta alerts
safety_and_rollback: Immediate rollback trigger if any of: +10% p95 latency, +5% median token-cost, or >0.5% error-rate increase
Graceful fallback: runtime will mark suggestion as 'unsafe' and revert to pinned model/kernel for that bucket
Audit log entries for every change in suggestion catalog with user and timestamp
experiments_and_validation: A/B experiment definitions for canary: treatment uses suggester picks, control uses current kernel picker
Statistical plan: p95 latency and token-cost as primary metrics, use sequential testing with alpha=0.01
Offline validation: run microbenchmarks across representative GPUs (A100, H100, L4) and sequence-length histograms
Comparison to baseline heuristics from ENG-47290 for cold-start behavior
